pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What do roots of cassava and sweet potato do besides taking in water? (1 mark)
   A. Make leaves
   B. Carry seeds
   C. Make flowers
   D. Store food

2. Which of these is a safety rule when handling plants? (1 mark)
   A. Pull plants with thorns barehanded
   B. Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   C. Rub sap on your eyes
   D. Taste every fruit you find

3. Which of these is a stem that stores food and is eaten or used for sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Sugarcane
   B. Tomato
   C. Bean pod
   D. Sukuma wiki leaf

4. A student says a tree is not alive because it does not move from place to place. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Only animals grow
   B. Trees are not plants
   C. Trees are made of stone
   D. Plants show life by growing and responding

5. What is the word for the tiny parts in a leaf where air goes in and out? (1 mark)
   A. Petals
   B. Seeds
   C. Tiny holes
   D. Roots

6. A sweet potato vine cutting grows roots and becomes a new plant. Which sign of life is shown? (1 mark)
   A. Dying
   B. Removing waste
   C. Reproducing
   D. Breathing out

7. Which of these is NOT alive? (1 mark)
   A. A plastic flower
   B. A young mango tree
   C. A grass blade
   D. A maize plant

8. A bat flies but has fur and feeds its babies milk. What is it? (1 mark)
   A. A bird
   B. A reptile
   C. An insect
   D. A mammal

9. Which of these is a vertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. Spider
   B. Hen
   C. Ant
   D. Snail

10. Why is a spider NOT an insect? (1 mark)
   A. It has eight legs, not six
   B. It has feathers
   C. It lives in water
   D. It has a backbone

11. What is the solid waste passed out through the anus called? (1 mark)
   A. Faeces
   B. Saliva
   C. Blood
   D. Juice

12. Which of these is a way of storing leftover food safely? (1 mark)
   A. Covering it and keeping it clean
   B. Putting it on the floor
   C. Sharing it with flies
   D. Leaving it uncovered in the sun

13. Which of these is a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Only soda
   B. Only tea
   C. Only sweets
   D. Ugali, vegetables and beans

14. What are the symptoms of worms mentioned in the lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Fast running
   B. Seeing worms in faeces, itchy anus, weakness
   C. Clear skin
   D. Loud voice

15. A pupil has hard dry faeces. Which is the best advice? (1 mark)
   A. Eat only white bread
   B. Eat more sweets
   C. Stop drinking water
   D. Eat more fruits, vegetables and drink water

16. Which food group helps to prevent constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Fizzy drinks
   B. Sweets
   C. Sugary biscuits
   D. Fibre in fruits and vegetables

17. What should you do when you have a persistent stomach ache? (1 mark)
   A. Drink dirty water
   B. Eat more sweets
   C. Hide it
   D. Tell an adult and see a health worker

18. What is the job of the anus? (1 mark)
   A. To let faeces leave the body
   B. To make saliva
   C. To digest food
   D. To swallow food

19. What is vomiting? (1 mark)
   A. Food coming out through the mouth
   B. Passing loose faeces
   C. Chewing food
   D. Feeling hungry

20. Which are the three states of matter? (1 mark)
   A. Big, medium and small
   B. Hot, warm and cold
   C. Hard, soft and rough
   D. Solid, liquid and gas

21. Which of these is matter? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Heat
   C. Light
   D. Sound

22. There are 750 ml of milk in a jug. 300 ml is poured out. How much is left? (1 mark)
   A. 450 ml
   B. 550 ml
   C. 1050 ml
   D. 350 ml

23. Which of these do we measure using litres? (1 mark)
   A. Mass of a book
   B. Time of a race
   C. Volume of juice
   D. Length of a rope

24. Which of these is heavier: 3 kg of sugar or 3000 g of sugar? (1 mark)
   A. Cannot tell
   B. They have the same mass
   C. 3000 g
   D. 3 kg

25. What happens to a liquid when you pour it into a different container? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes a solid
   B. It disappears
   C. It keeps its old shape
   D. It takes the shape of the new container

26. Which is the best way to manage the food remains from the school kitchen? (1 mark)
   A. Put them in a compost pit
   B. Burn them near classrooms
   C. Throw them in a river
   D. Bury plastic with them

27. What does reuse mean? (1 mark)
   A. Burn it
   B. Throw it away
   C. Bury it
   D. Use something again

28. A tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much is wasted in 5 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 25 litres
   B. 10 litres
   C. 7 litres
   D. 2 litres

29. Which of these holds a shirt together? (1 mark)
   A. Oil
   B. Thread stitches
   C. A rolling wheel
   D. Wind

30. Logs placed under a heavy load help it move because they act as (1 mark)
   A. Brakes
   B. Rollers
   C. Weights
   D. Glue

31. Why do we put oil on machine parts? (1 mark)
   A. To reduce friction
   B. To make them heavy
   C. To increase friction
   D. To make them weak

32. Which of these will make a block slide the shortest distance on a ramp? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Oiled plastic
   C. Sandpaper
   D. Smooth tile

33. Why do some farmers use bright lights near animal pens at night? (1 mark)
   A. To make animals heavier
   B. To make animals sleepy
   C. To scare away wild animals
   D. To warm animals

34. What does a translucent roof sheet do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes light
   B. Creates sound
   C. Blocks all light
   D. Lets some light in

35. Which of these could you use to test three cards for straight line travel of light? (1 mark)
   A. A bell
   B. Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
   C. A cup of water
   D. A ruler only

36. Why do farmers dry maize in the sun before storing it? (1 mark)
   A. So it becomes heavier
   B. So it becomes wetter
   C. So it does not rot or grow mould
   D. So it starts to grow

37. In which unit is temperature measured in science? (1 mark)
   A. Litres
   B. Degrees Celsius
   C. Kilograms
   D. Metres

38. If you smell gas from a cooker, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Tell an adult and keep flames away
   C. Turn on an electric switch
   D. Light a match

39. Why should kitchen gloves be dry? (1 mark)
   A. Wet cloth is thicker
   B. Dry cloth is heavier
   C. Dry cloth is colder
   D. Wet cloth passes heat quickly

40. Which of these sources of heat uses electricity? (1 mark)
   A. Firewood
   B. The sun
   C. Charcoal jiko
   D. Electric iron

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why plants are called living things. (3 marks)

42. List the five groups of vertebrates and give one example of each. (3 marks)

43. Explain the difference between reducing and reusing water. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

44. State two ways of reducing friction. (2 marks)

45. Classify these as natural or artificial: candle, stars, torch, lightning, firefly, solar lamp. (4 marks)

46. Make a plan for keeping your digestive system healthy for one week. (5 marks)

47. Explain why heat from the sun is important to the Earth. (3 marks)

48. Compare solids, liquids and gases in terms of shape and volume. (4 marks)

49. Describe how a wheelbarrow makes work easier and how it is looked after. (4 marks)

50. Explain how drip irrigation and mulching save water. (4 marks)

51. Give three ways of caring for animals. (3 marks)

52. Explain how ball bearings help a bicycle move. (4 marks)

53. Give two ways of reducing waste at home. (2 marks)

54. A shopkeeper has 2 kg of sugar and 750 g of salt. Find the total mass in grams. (3 marks)

55. What is evaporation? Give one example. (2 marks)

56. Explain why sorting waste is important for reusing and recycling. (4 marks)

57. Describe an experiment to show that a solid keeps its shape but a liquid takes the shape of its container. State what you would observe. (5 marks)

58. State two uses of heat at home. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Store food
   These roots store food for the plant.

2. B — Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   Some plants can hurt or poison people, so ask first.

3. A — Sugarcane
   Sugarcane stems store sugar.

4. D — Plants show life by growing and responding
   Plants show many signs of life even though they do not walk.

5. C — Tiny holes
   Air moves in and out of leaves through tiny holes.

6. C — Reproducing
   Making a new plant from part of an old plant is reproduction.

7. A — A plastic flower
   A plastic flower is made by people and does not grow, respond or reproduce.

8. D — A mammal
   The fur and milk feeding make it a mammal.

9. B — Hen
   A hen is a bird and has a backbone.

10. A — It has eight legs, not six
   Insects have six legs and spiders have eight.

11. A — Faeces
   Faeces are the solid waste of the body.

12. A — Covering it and keeping it clean
   Covered food is safer from germs.

13. D — Ugali, vegetables and beans
   A balanced meal has energy foods, body-building foods and protective foods.

14. B — Seeing worms in faeces, itchy anus, weakness
   These are signs that worms may be present.

15. D — Eat more fruits, vegetables and drink water
   Fibre and water help soften faeces.

16. D — Fibre in fruits and vegetables
   Fibre helps food move through the intestines.

17. D — Tell an adult and see a health worker
   Adults and health workers can help find the cause.

18. A — To let faeces leave the body
   The anus is the opening at the end of the digestive tube.

19. A — Food coming out through the mouth
   Vomiting is throwing up food through the mouth.

20. D — Solid, liquid and gas
   Matter exists as solids, liquids and gases.

21. A — Water
   Water has mass and takes up space. Light, sound and heat are not matter.

22. A — 450 ml
   750 - 300 = 450 ml.

23. C — Volume of juice
   Litres measure volume.

24. B — They have the same mass
   3 kg equals 3000 g.

25. D — It takes the shape of the new container
   A liquid has no shape of its own.

26. A — Put them in a compost pit
   Kitchen waste can be composted.

27. D — Use something again
   To reuse is to use again.

28. B — 10 litres
   2 x 5 = 10 litres.

29. B — Thread stitches
   Stitches hold cloth pieces together.

30. B — Rollers
   Rollers reduce friction.

31. A — To reduce friction
   Oil makes surfaces slide easily.

32. C — Sandpaper
   Rough surfaces have the most friction.

33. C — To scare away wild animals
   Bright lights can scare away predators.

34. D — Lets some light in
   It lets daylight in but you cannot see through it clearly.

35. B — Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
   Aligned holes let light pass only when straight.

36. C — So it does not rot or grow mould
   Heat dries the grain and dry grain keeps longer.

37. B — Degrees Celsius
   Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

38. B — Tell an adult and keep flames away
   Gas can catch fire, so avoid flames.

39. D — Wet cloth passes heat quickly
   Wet cloth can burn your hand.

40. D — Electric iron
   An electric iron uses electricity.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: They show signs of life. They grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes and die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying they show signs of life and 2 marks for correct signs given.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mammals (goat), birds (hen), reptiles (snake), amphibians (frog), fish (tilapia).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for correct five groups, 1 mark for four examples, 1 mark for correct matching.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reducing means using less water, for example closing the tap. Reusing means using the same water again, for example using washing water for the garden.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for examples.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Smoothen surfaces, use oil or grease, use rollers, use ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Natural: stars, lightning, firefly. Artificial: candle, torch, solar lamp.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair, plus 1 mark for correct table.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan including brushing teeth twice a day, eating fruits and vegetables, drinking clean water, washing hands, chewing well, deworming as advised and limiting sweets.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible action up to 5.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: It warms the Earth so plants and animals can live, it dries things, and helps the water cycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solid: own shape and fixed volume. Liquid: takes shape of container, fixed volume. Gas: no shape and no fixed volume, fills the container.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each state with correct shape and volume, plus 1 mark for a comparison.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: The wheel rolls so friction with the ground is small. It is easier to push than drag a load. Oil the joints and wheel axle to reduce friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for wheel, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for oil, 1 mark for care.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drip irrigation sends water drop by drop to the roots so little is lost. Mulch covers soil so less water evaporates.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each method.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide shelter, keep their homes clean, treat sick animals, do not beat them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: They are small steel balls in the wheel. They roll between moving parts, so there is less friction and the wheels turn easily.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what they are, 1 mark for rolling, 1 mark for less friction, 1 mark for wheels turning easily.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Buy less packaging, carry a reusable bag, cook only what is needed, repair things.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2750 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 2 kg = 2000 g, 1 mark for adding 750 g and 1 mark for the answer.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Liquid water turning into water vapour, for example wet clothes drying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for an example.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sorting separates plastics, metals, glass, paper and food waste so each can be recycled, reused or composted without contaminating the others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sorting, 1 mark for recycling, 1 mark for composting, 1 mark for clear link.

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: Use a stone and water. Put the stone in a cup and then in a bowl. It keeps its shape. Pour water in the cup and then into the bowl and its shape changes with the container. Conclusion: solids keep shape but liquids take the container's shape.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for stone in both containers, 1 mark for water in both, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Cooking, warming, ironing, drying clothes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
